deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and neighbouring pages. X is a surface with a cell structure, essentially the real projective plane, carrying an arrangement Σ of pseudolines. 𝒳 is the space of pseudolines D in general position with respect to Σ. It is a cell complex whose cells are combinatorial types of D relative to Σ, i.e. a topological model of the space of one-element extensions of the arrangement. F = F_D denotes the base point / fibre structure attached to D.

For each D there are three {±1}-torsors:
- ω(D) ≅ ω(F): the local orientations of the ambient surface X along D;
- Σ_s(D): the choices of side of D, i.e. local co-orientations;
- Σ_o(D): the orientations of D itself.

A path c in 𝒳 from D to D' induces isomorphisms between the corresponding torsors at D and D'. The isomorphism ω_X(c) comes from parallel transport over X (previous page). Because orientation of the surface = orientation of the line ∧ co-orientation, i.e. ω ≅ Σ_s ∧ Σ_o, any two of these transports determine the third. Passing to monodromy characters π_1(𝒳,F) → {±1} gives χ_X = χ_s χ_o, written symmetrically as χ_X χ_s χ_o = 1.

Two further characters are introduced:
- χ_𝒳: the orientation character of the cell complex 𝒳;
- χ_c: a 'combinatorial' character given by the parity par(c) of the number of walls crossed by c (its 'poids').

Comparing the orientation transport of 𝒳 with that of X gives ω_𝒳(c) = par(c)·ω_X(c). The local system of χ_c has fibres {±1} and transition maps par(c). Hence χ_𝒳 = χ_X χ_c (as stated a few lines later). So there are three independent fundamental characters, chosen as χ_X, χ_s, χ_c, with χ_o = χ_X χ_s and χ_𝒳 = χ_X χ_c.

Programme announced: compute these characters, together with the representation u: π_1(𝒳,F_D) → Aut(Pℓ(D)), on fundamental loops. Here Pℓ(D) is the induced cell structure on the circle D, with dihedral automorphism group. A marginal note, proved on the next page, says χ_c = 1. The reason is that the parity of a path from D to D' equals sing(D') − sing(D) mod 2, where sing(D) is the number of vertices of Σ lying on D. Hence χ_𝒳 = χ_X: the orientation character of the space of pseudolines equals the orientation monodromy of the plane along the moving line. The next page also shows u is surjective onto the dihedral group.

Purpose: understand the topology (orientability, monodromy) of the space of pseudoline extensions of an arrangement.
errors: The boxed formula χ_𝒳 = χ_o χ_c contradicts the line just above it, ω_𝒳(c) = par(c) ω_X(c), which gives χ_𝒳 = χ_X χ_c. Grothendieck himself writes χ_𝒳 = χ_X χ_c a few lines later and χ_𝒳 = χ_X (written χ_×) on the next page. The box is a slip, or a misreading of the subscript.
χ_c is listed as one of three independent fundamental characters, but the marginal note and the next page show χ_c ≡ 1. So only two characters are independent; Grothendieck corrects himself.

ideas.what: Monodromy characters of the {±1}-torsors (ambient orientation, co-orientation, line orientation) along loops in a space of pseudolines, with relation χ_X = χ_s χ_o
ideas.modern_name: orientation local systems / first Stiefel–Whitney classes; w1(TX|D) = w1(TD) + w1(ND)

ideas.what: Orientation character of the cell space 𝒳 of pseudolines relative to an arrangement, expressed as χ_X times a wall-crossing parity character (later shown trivial)
ideas.modern_name: orientability of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (single-element extensions)

ideas.what: Monodromy representation u: π_1(𝒳,F_D) → Aut(Pℓ(D)) on the induced cell structure of the moving pseudoline
ideas.modern_name: monodromy of the cut-point configuration on an extending pseudoline (dihedral action)

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck treats the space of pseudolines extending a given arrangement as a cell complex and studies its fundamental group, orientation character and monodromy. This is a topological study of what is now called the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid, before Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993) and the extension-space conjecture literature.
missed.quote: En plus de ces trois caractères, il y en a deux autres, χ_𝒳 = caractère d'orientation de 𝒳 ... (défini par la structure cellulaire), et χ_c ("combinatoire")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Provides an early independent approach to extension spaces and the orientability of their cell structure. Of mainly historical interest, since the rank-3 topology is now understood.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is careful bookkeeping of {±1}-characters and contains a small slip. Its interest lies in the context: an unpublished early study of the topology of pseudoline extension spaces, anticipating later oriented-matroid work, though nothing deep is proved on this page.
transcription_corrections: The boxed formula reads χ_𝒳 = χ_o χ_c. It is inconsistent with the later line χ_𝒳 = χ_X χ_c, which should be kept as written.
The marginal note at right reads 'On a χ_c = 1, cf ... !', referring to the proof on the next page.
In 'Ces iso. ne sont pas indépendants', the words 'deux à deux' are doubtful; the sense is 'puisque deux déterminent le troisième'.
The diagonal marginal note is largely illegible. It seems to concern χ_s: 'pour χ_s ... il faut voir les ... naturelles ...'. Its transcription should be treated as conjectural.
